title: Telling Better Stories
description: Use narrative tense control to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to telling better stories with appropriate B2 complexity.
objectives: Use narrative tense control to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to telling better stories with appropriate B2 complexity.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use narrative tense control to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to telling better stories with appropriate B2 complexity. The central language focus is narrative tense control. In the context of advanced storytelling, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B2, organize the message so the listener can follow the claim, support, qualification, and practical consequence. Choose collocations and discourse markers that sound natural in professional and social contexts.

blocks.english: We should consider compelling account carefully.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.
This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “We should consider compelling account carefully.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “The discussion highlighted vivid detail.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: narrative tense control. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by narrative tense control; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For telling better stories, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

In this situation, The discussion highlighted vivid detail. A clear explanation addresses sequence of events directly.
From another perspective, A clear explanation addresses sequence of events directly. The speaker emphasized had already happened.
More specifically, The speaker emphasized had already happened. Our response should account for by the time.
Even so, Our response should account for by the time. This example illustrates set the scene clearly.
As a result, This example illustrates set the scene clearly. We should consider in the distance carefully.
